source.generation: Higgsfield image_to_3d (Meshy), single reference image, should_texture=true, enable_pbr=true, then gltf-transform optimize (--compress false, --texture-compress auto --texture-size 1024, --simplify --simplify-ratio 0.4)

knownLimitations: Generated LYING FLAT (thin axis on Y/height instead of Z/depth) — a distinct defect from the usual proportion miss seen elsewhere this session. A round mirror photographed face-on gives the model no cue that it should hang upright, so it reconstructed it as a disc resting on the floor. Corrected with a one-off -90deg rotation about X (scripts/_rotate_tmp.py, not checked in — see delivery notes) before running the usual fit_glb.py height fit. This is a lossless root-node transform, same pattern as fit_to_height.

After the orientation fix and height fit, PASSES the automated check cleanly: measured 80.0 x 80.0 x 3.2 cm against the real 80 x 80 x 4 cm (0cm/0.8cm off, well within tolerance). The circular symmetry made this an easy fix once the orientation was caught.
